q1.answer: No, ADR013 (node-fetch) is superseded by ADR014. ADR014 says frontend plugins/packages should prefer fetchApiRef (and that code running in Node.js itself should use native fetch, with typeof fetch as the TS type); isomorphic packages should depend on cross-fetch and accept an injected typeof fetch.

q2.answer: ADR007 (Use MSW to mock http requests) requires any fetch/XMLHTTPRequest in tests to be mocked with msw's express-style route handlers across the whole repo. It's meant to avoid each test having its own one-off, inconsistent mocking implementation, and to avoid mocking fetch directly (which react-testing-library recommends against).

q3.answer: ADR006 cites that React.FC implicitly adds a children prop, and does not support generic types on children. It notes that Facebook removed React.FC from the create-react-app TypeScript base template as a concrete fact about it falling out of favor.

q4.answer: ADR010 names Moment.js as the library Luxon replaces. The two reasons given are that Moment.js suffers from large bundle size and mutable state issues, and that the Moment.js project itself is being sunset/recommends alternatives.

q5.answer: ADR004 (Module export structure) requires every exported symbol to be traceable through index files all the way to the package root src/index.ts (each index file only re-exporting its own immediate children). It was meant to make it easy to answer "is this export also exported by the package?" / "what is exported from this directory?"

q6.answer: No, under ADR004's rule they are not part of the public API: the rule works by tracing index files toward the root, and if any index file in the chain (here there is no src/utils/index.ts and src/index.ts doesn't mention them) fails to re-export the symbol, it is considered not publicly exported, even without any explicit private marker.

q7.answer: ADR011 says x-react packages are for shared widgets, hooks, and similar code that both the plugin itself and third-party frontend plugins can depend on. Notifications would need such components/hooks (e.g. its hooks or RelativeTime-style components) actually be consumed by other, third-party frontend plugins before an x-react split would be justified.

q8.answer: ADR003 allows default exports only for React.lazy modules. For teams wanting to avoid even that, it gives the workaround of wrapping a named export, e.g. `React.lazy(() => import('../path/to/Component').then(m => ({ default: m.Component })))`.

q9.answer: ADR015 defines the loader/component (and element/component) option pattern. Its Consequences section says it will be applied to new APIs in the new frontend system (@backstage/frontend-* packages) but will NOT be retrofitted onto existing APIs in the old frontend system (@backstage/core-* packages), which is the style the dev app predates/follows.
